blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's e-mail, name, phone and postal address) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
findings.recommendation: The proposal promises that the button "erases the member's personal data", but delete_account only soft-deletes: it sets deleted_at and clears password_hash, while the users row keeps email, display_name, phone and postal_address (app/schema.sql:3-6). Scenario: a member clicks "Delete my account"; their e-mail, name, phone and postal address stay in the users table indefinitely, still joined to their orders through orders.user_id — the right to erasure (GDPR Art. 17) and storage limitation (Art. 5(1)(e)) are not met. Overwrite or NULL every personal column (e.g. set email to a unique non-identifying placeholder such as 'deleted-<id>' since it is NOT NULL UNIQUE, display_name to a fixed value, phone and postal_address to NULL) so orders keep only the opaque user id, add a test asserting those columns no longer hold the member's data, and state how long backups keep the erased data before they expire.
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's e-mail, name, phone and postal address

findings.recommendation: The change adds a pseudonymous analytics identifier derived deterministically from the user id and a fixed salt, but delete_account does nothing about the analytics events it keys: after deletion, anyone holding the salt can still link those events back to the kept users row (pseudonymised data is still personal data). The analytics store and its callers are not visible in this repository, so this depends on what it holds. Either erase or detach the member's analytics events on deletion, or document that they are anonymised (e.g. salt rotation) and their retention period; also state its purpose and lawful basis, since nothing in the change uses it yet.
findings.title: Analytics events keyed by analytics_id are not reached by the erasure
